single-column theme browser; each item = primary label stacked over a row of 5 circular color chips (theme palette preview); selected row = flat gray full-width band (defect); 'list options' table that should carry a checkmark
export canvas: full-bleed saturated color field as preview stage, dashed rounded-rect crop guide, rendered code card with own decorative traffic lights + soft drop shadow
no real toolbar; single centered pop-up ('swift' language selector) as titlebar accessory; genuine colored traffic lights (focused)

signature_moves: Swatch-row theme browser: each of 80+ themes previewed as name + five circular color chips instead of full code thumbnails — scan-by-color-signature, a Hick's-Law reduction at the theme-picking decision point
Full-bleed saturated color canvas as export stage: the background/padding setting promoted to ~half the window, making the rendered snapshot the unambiguous focal object (Von Restorff)
defects: Contrast Dilution — theme-list selection is a #DCDCDD band on #FFFFFF (~1.1:1), colour-only, no accent tint/checkmark; canon = inset rounded accent-tinted fill with accent text, or a persistent checkmark for a list-options table
Accent not bound — selection/focus use gray, controlAccentColor never bound (theme chips are legitimate separate identity colours)
Internal selection inconsistency — sidebar uses inset-rounded selection while content list uses a full-width flat band; two grammars in one window

aesthetic.direction: platform-default / system-native utilitarian (stock AppKit, near-zero custom styling) — while the marketing panel is a restrained Swiss / neo-grotesque brand voice (bold grotesk wordmark, two-tone headline, monochrome icons on cool off-white, colour supplied only by the product screenshot)

psychology: Hick's Law — swatch-row theme list lets users scan 80+ themes by color signature rather than reading names or parsing previews, shortening the one real decision (theme pick)
Von Restorff / signal-detection — single saturated orange canvas makes the rendered code card the clear focal object against neutral chrome; the one loud thing is the output
Jakob's Law — three-pane source-list layout matches trained macOS expectations (Mail/Finder/System Settings), so navigation is predictable
Aesthetic-Usability limit (violated) — ~1.1:1 selection contrast is a fluency snag: 'which theme is selected?' is momentarily ambiguous
notes: Single input = marketing cover only (no gallery shots; meta gallery empty). Left half is brand/marketing (wordmark, headline, monochrome feature-icon list) — recorded separately, excluded from app-UI + macOS canon. Right half is the app window on a Big Sur gradient backdrop (backdrop = marketing/desktop, not chrome). Window rendered ~@1x and cropped right+bottom, so pixel metrics are estimated (colours measured). Two values that must NOT be learned as chrome: canvas/export-bg #FF4406 and codecard/bg #222323 are user-chosen export/content, not app design tokens. No settings/empty-state/dark-mode/onboarding surface seen. Lineage native (high); era Big Sur legacy (med-high) — the pre-capsule pop-up + flat gray chrome + absence of any glass/scroll-edge date it before Tahoe. Icon (icon.webp) is a separate Workflow-B subject, not digested here.
